title: God Rays Volumetric Light Scattering with Save/Load State
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with Three.js that implements volumetric light scattering (god rays) as a post-processing effect with full save/load state functionality.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use Three.js r152+ with EffectComposer for post-processing
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 20), FOV 60, looking at origin
- A bright emissive sphere (radius 1.5) at position (0, 8, -15) representing the sun/light source, color #FFE4B5
- 5 occluder objects (dark cubes of size 2x4x2) placed at positions: (-6,2,0), (-3,3,-2), (0,1,1), (3,4,-1), (6,2,0)
- A ground plane (50x50) at y=0 with a dark gray material
- Ambient light intensity 0.1, no other scene lights (god rays provide illumination feel)

GOD RAYS POST-PROCESSING:
- Implement a custom ShaderPass for volumetric light scattering
- The shader must use the standard light scattering algorithm: sample along ray from each pixel toward light source screen position, accumulate occluded light
- Parameters (all adjustable): decay (default 0.96), exposure (default 0.22), density (default 0.8), weight (default 0.6), numSamples (default 80)
- The light source screen position must be computed each frame by projecting the sun sphere's world position to NDC
- Render an occlusion texture: render scene with occluders as black and light source as white to a separate render target

USER INTERACTIONS:
- Keyboard 'W'/'S': Move camera forward/backward by 1 unit along its look direction
- Keyboard 'A'/'D': Orbit camera left/right around origin by 5 degrees
- Keyboard '1'-'5': Toggle visibility of occluder cubes (1=leftmost, 5=rightmost)
- Keyboard 'R': Reset all parameters to defaults
- Mouse wheel: Adjust exposure parameter (up = +0.02, down = -0.02), clamped [0.01, 1.0]
- DOM slider '#decay-slider': Range 0.8 to 1.0, step 0.01, controls decay parameter
- DOM slider '#density-slider': Range 0.1 to 2.0, step 0.1, controls density parameter
- DOM slider '#weight-slider': Range 0.1 to 1.5, step 0.1, controls weight parameter
- DOM slider '#samples-slider': Range 10 to 150, step 10, controls numSamples (integer)
- DOM button '#save-state': Saves current state to localStorage key 'godRaysState'
- DOM button '#load-state': Loads state from localStorage key 'godRaysState' and applies it
- DOM button '#undo-btn': Reverts to the previous state (maintain a history stack of max 20 entries)
- DOM button '#redo-btn': Re-applies a state that was undone

SAVE/LOAD STATE:
- State includes: all 5 shader parameters, camera position (x,y,z), camera orbit angle, all 5 occluder visibility booleans
- Every parameter change pushes to history stack
- Save serializes current state as JSON to localStorage
- Load deserializes and applies all values (camera moves, sliders update, shader uniforms update)
- Undo/Redo navigate the history stack without pushing new entries

HUD/UI:
- A panel at top-right showing current values: exposure, decay, density, weight, numSamples
- Display camera orbit angle in degrees
- Display history stack size and current index
- All sliders and buttons in a left-side panel with labels

STATE MANAGEMENT - window.__3D_STATE__ must expose:
- exposure: current exposure value (number)
- decay: current decay value (number)
- density: current density value (number)
- weight: current weight value (number)
- numSamples: current numSamples (integer)
- cameraPosition: {x, y, z} camera world position
- cameraOrbitAngle: orbit angle in degrees
- occluderVisibility: [bool, bool, bool, bool, bool] for cubes 1-5
- lightScreenPos: {x, y} NDC of projected light source (-1 to 1 range)
- historyIndex: current index in history stack
- historyLength: total entries in history stack
- lastSavedState: the JSON string last saved (or null)
- lastLoadedState: the JSON string last loaded (or null)
- frameCount: incremented each render frame
- sunWorldPos: {x, y, z} sun position
- undoCount: number of undo operations performed
- redoCount: number of redo operations performed
physics_constraints: Light scattering must follow physically-based accumulation: each sample along the ray multiplies by decay factor. Exposure must clamp to [0.01, 1.0]. Camera orbit must wrap at 360 degrees. History stack must not exceed 20 entries (oldest removed when full). NDC light position must be mathematically correct projection of world position.
